```{r}
#| label: setup

library(plotly)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
```

## Popularity: Molly vs. Michael (Top Male Name in 1991)

```{r}
#| label: name-comparison

# Read baby name files and extract the year from the filename
files <- list.files("data", pattern = "^yob.*\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

babies <- read_csv(
  files,
  id = "file",
  col_names = c("name", "sex", "n"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(year = parse_number(basename(file)))

# Identify the most popular male name in 1991
top_male_1991 <- babies |>
  filter(year == 1991, sex == "M") |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1) |>
  pull(name)

# Filter both names for the last 50 years and aggregate counts
comp_data <- babies |>
  filter(name %in% c("Molly", top_male_1991), year >= 1976) |>
  group_by(name, year) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(tooltip = paste0("Name: ", name, "\nYear: ", year, "\nBabies: ", comma(n)))

# Build side-by-side comparison with independent y-axes
p <- ggplot(comp_data, aes(x = year, y = n, color = name, text = tooltip, group = name)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Michael" = "#d95f02", "Molly" = "#2b5c8f")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2020, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Popularity Trend: Molly vs.", top_male_1991, "(1976–2025)"),
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Babies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Interactive plot with hover tooltips
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text")
```

In 1991, the most popular male name was **Michael** with 61,077 babies, coinciding with Molly's peak year of 4,663 babies. While Molly rose sharply through the 1980s before tapering off, Michael was undergoing a long, steady decline from over 67,000 in 1976 to around 8,100 in 2025.
